problem: VLNCE policies (e.g., ETPNav, BEVBert) are sensitive to camera height and viewing-angle changes, so performance drops sharply when the camera differs from training. Prior work (GVNav) only retrains for one fixed ground-level height with a two-stage pipeline, and manipulation view-invariance methods need costly pre-training.
motivation: Real robots mount cameras at different heights and angles, so deployed policies must handle viewpoint shifts. Retraining from scratch for every embodiment is expensive and discards VLN pretraining. The paper therefore adapts existing pretrained policies to varied viewpoints with a lightweight post-training step.
key_idea: Post-train a pretrained VLNCE policy end-to-end with a contrastive loss aligning standard and varied-viewpoint panoramic features, plus a teacher-student KL distillation of a waypoint predictor whose only trainable part is its input layer.
insight: Simple retraining on varied viewpoints is insufficient (varied-view val-unseen SPL only +0.7 and standard-view SPL -1.2 in the ablation). The waypoint predictor distillation matters most (removing it drops val-unseen SPL by 8.3 under varied viewpoints), and contrastive learning adds a further ~2.8 SPL. Gains hold on OOD viewpoints and reduce the std across 81 viewpoints (SPL std 10.79 to 3.59).
method: V2-VLNCE setting: each episode samples a camera height offset from U[-0.5m,0.5m] and a pitch angle from U[-30°,30°] relative to the standard config, evaluated on R2R-CE and RxR-CE.

Contrastive view-invariant learning: a shared encoder plus a 3-layer SimCLRv2-style projection head; g1 (identity-initialized) gives task features and g3(g2(g1)) gives contrastive features. InfoNCE (tau=1.0) uses same-heading standard/varied pairs as positives, and cross-scene batch-shift negatives plus opposite-heading (j+6) intra-scene hard negatives.
Feature mixing: the graph representation uses standard or varied task features, sampled with probability p1=0.1.

Teacher-student waypoint distillation: a frozen teacher waypoint predictor sees standard views, and a student with the same architecture sees varied views. Only the student's original input linear layer is trainable, and a KL divergence between softmax logits is minimized.
Teacher/student prediction sampling: the local topological graph is built from teacher or student waypoints with probability p2=0.1 for the teacher.

Joint end-to-end objective: L = L_nav + 0.2 L_cl + 10 L_wpd, initialized from official ETPNav/BEVBert checkpoints. The student alone is used at inference, and post-training takes ~48h (~14% of the full ETPNav training time).

setting.backbone: ETPNav and BEVBert (pretrained checkpoints, post-trained with VIL); waypoint predictor student with trainable input layer
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE training splits rendered with random varied viewpoints; no extra data
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 RGB + 12 depth views at 30° intervals)
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints on a topological map (ETPNav-style high-level, continuous environment)

numbers.extra: evaluated under V2-VLNCE varied viewpoints (height ±0.5m, angle ±30°)

numbers_note: Table 1 values are integer-rounded as printed for nDTW/OSR/SR/SPL. Ablation, robot-placement, OOD and real-robot tables are not included as separate entries. Real-robot SR (Office 28 to 44, Lounge 20 to 48) is a small proof of concept.
results: On V2-VLNCE, ETPNav+VIL improves SR by 8-15 points over ETPNav on R2R-CE (val-unseen 47 to 55) and by 11-15 on RxR-CE (val-unseen 39 to 50). It also beats GVNav on ground-level val-unseen (SR 57 vs 55) without matched training. Under the standard viewpoint VIL keeps or slightly improves accuracy, e.g. RxR-CE val-unseen SR 55.6 / SPL 46.2 vs ETPNav 53.8 / 43.9.
limitations: The real-robot evaluation is small (2 environments, 5 instructions x 5 starts) and uses a panoramic RGB + LiDAR rig rather than a typical monocular camera.
Only camera height and pitch are varied (a bounded range of ±0.5m and ±30°); roll, FOV and other embodiment differences are not covered, and the RxR-CE ablation is omitted.
Evaluated only on ETPNav and BEVBert (panoramic waypoint-based architectures), so generality to other VLN architectures is untested.
